owasp.subtitle: A Top 10 (2021) posture report written by the configured model, from what the scanners found.

quality.title: Quality
quality.subtitle: What source analysis reports about how the code is written, rather than about how safe it is.
quality.quality_notice: These findings never fail a build. They are visible, exportable, and have no say in the continuous-integration gate.

reachability.reachable_desc: Analysis linked this component to code that is called. The vulnerability is not merely present in the dependency tree: it sits on an execution path.
reachability.unreachable_desc: A person established that this component is not on an execution path. Static analysis alone never concludes this way: absence of a matched call is not proof of absence.

rule_sets.title: Semgrep rule sets
rule_sets.subtitle: Vectispire ships one rule; the public sets are not redistributable, so source-code coverage comes from a set you install here. What you upload travels with every scan, including to remote agents.
rule_sets.yaml_hint: YAML only. A folder is walked whole and everything that is not a rule file is left behind — said below, never in silence. Nothing is sent until you upload.
rule_sets.ignored_files: file(s) without a .yaml or .yml extension were ignored.
rule_sets.no_rules_found: No rule was found in the selected files.
rule_sets.delete_confirm: Are you sure you want to delete this rule set?

schedule.cron_hint: Five fields — minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. 0 2 * * * is every day at 02:00, 0 */6 * * * every six hours. The server refuses an expression it cannot read, so a mistake here is reported rather than saved.
schedule.cron_wins: Both are set, so the cron expression is what runs. The interval stays on the target and takes over again if the expression is cleared.
schedule.cron_wins_warning: Both are set: the cron schedule wins and the interval is ignored.
schedule.interval_hint: Counted from the end of the last scheduled round, so it drifts: use a cron expression when the hour matters.
schedule.manual_only: Both are empty: this target is scanned only when somebody asks. There is no default schedule.
schedule.manual_only_warning: Neither interval nor cron: this target will only be scanned on request.

security.subtitle: The verdict the continuous-integration gate would return for each target, with the policy that produced it.
security.unobserved_warn: Some targets have not been observed. An empty backlog passes every policy: their verdict says nothing until a scan has succeeded.

ssh_keys.generation_notice: Generating a pair from the interface is not ported yet. Generate one with ssh-keygen -t ed25519, then paste the private half here.
ssh_keys.name: Name
ssh_keys.private_key_hint: Encrypted with AES-256-GCM before writing to the database, under ENCRYPTION_KEY. The clear key is never stored and never returned over this API.
ssh_keys.public_key_hint: Optional, but recommended: it allows Vectispire to display the key's fingerprint without having to decrypt its private half.
ssh_keys.delete_confirm: Are you sure you want to delete this key? Repositories using it will fail to clone on their next scan.

encryption_status.current_hint: Encrypted with the current encryption key.
encryption_status.previous_key_hint: Encrypted with a previous encryption key. Save it again to move it under ENCRYPTION_KEY — and if it dates from the default key published in the repository, its private half is public: generate a new pair.
encryption_status.unreadable_hint: No configured key decrypts this value: the next clone that needs it will fail. Add the previous key to VECTISPIRE_PREVIOUS_ENCRYPTION_KEYS, or replace this SSH key.

exceptions.title: Exceptions register
exceptions.subtitle: What somebody decided not to fix, and under what terms. A clean backlog means two very different things depending on whether it was cleared or argued away.
exceptions.empty: No exception has been granted or requested.
exceptions.footnote: Fixes are not listed here. An issue closed because it was repaired is not an exception, and merging the two would bury these few rows under every resolution the estate has ever made.

review_dialog.title: Review an exception
review_dialog.help: Confirming changes nothing, and that is the point: it records that somebody looked. Without it, an acceptance revisited each quarter and one nobody has opened since read identically.

outcome.confirmed_help: Unchanged. The entry exists so that “somebody looked” is a dated fact.
outcome.extended: It still holds, with a new date
outcome.revoked: It does not hold any more
outcome.revoked_help: The issue goes back under review and the gate stops honouring the exception.

exceptions.load_failed: Could not load the exceptions register.

gate_verdicts.title: Verdict register
gate_verdicts.subtitle: What the gate answered, newest first. A refusal is the only proof a control runs: “every target passes” does not distinguish a clean estate from a gate that has never stopped anything.
gate_verdicts.empty: The gate has not answered yet.
gate_verdicts.empty_refusals: The gate has refused nothing in this window.
gate_verdicts.footnote: Verdicts are kept for the evidence retention window. A “passed” verdict over zero examined issues is shown as such: it proves nothing but the absence of anything to judge.
gate_verdicts.load_failed: Could not load the verdict register.

delays.title: Time to fix
delays.subtitle: An average is dragged down by the volume of easy fixes. What describes a process is the share that met its deadline, the tail of the distribution, and the age of the oldest item still open.
delays.oldest_open_help: No average can show this line.
delays.no_deadline_help: No deadline set — a percentage against an absent rule would not be one.
delays.empty: Nothing has been resolved in this window.
delays.footnote: The 90th percentile is at nearest rank: it is a duration an issue really had, not a point interpolated between two. Issues closed in the instant they were seen are absent from the distribution rather than sitting at its floor.

unconfigured.title: Code analysis covers one pattern, in Python.
unconfigured.body: The repositories in other languages are not analysed — no rule reaches them, so a zero here means nothing was looked for.

partial.title: No rule covers:
partial.body: Injection and SSRF are not measured there — those categories are not green, they are without evidence.

soa.title: Statement of applicability
soa.subtitle: What the organisation claims about each control, set against what the estate measures. The useful artefact is neither half: it is the line where the two disagree.
soa.incomplete_notice: Clause 6.1.3 d asks for every Annex A control to be addressed — applicable or excluded. A control nobody has written a line for is a gap, not a blank.

divergence_help.CONTRADICTED: Declared implemented; measured non-compliant. Not merely short of a control — the opposite was stated in writing.
divergence_help.EXCLUDED_WITHOUT_JUSTIFICATION: Clause 6.1.3 d allows an exclusion and requires it to be argued.
divergence_help.UNDECLARED: The framework has this control and the declaration does not mention it.
divergence_help.UNDERSTATED: Declared planned or not implemented; measured compliant. The document has drifted behind the practice.
divergence_help.NOT_MEASURED_HERE: Evidence lives outside this product, so nothing here bears on the claim.
divergence_help.NOT_APPLICABLE: Excluded with a justification. Nothing to reconcile.
divergence_help.CONSISTENT: The declaration and the measurement agree.

dialog.title: Declare a control
dialog.evidence_help: Vectispire measures a slice of each control, never the whole of it. A control evidenced elsewhere is not judged against what is measured here.
dialog.external_evidence: Name the document, register or review
dialog.justification_required: Required: clause 6.1.3 d does not accept an unargued exclusion.

soa.load_failed: Could not load the statement of applicability.

scope.title: Certified scope
scope.subtitle: What the management system's certified scope covers, and how much of it carries current evidence. A tool measuring its own coverage always reports full coverage — this one measures against the scope document instead.
scope.undeclared_notice: Nobody has said how many assets the scope covers, so coverage here is measured against what this instance happens to hold. Set “Assets the certified scope covers” in the settings to make the gap visible.
scope.unaccounted: assets the scope claims that this instance holds no row for
scope.unaccounted_help: They cannot be scanned, cannot be counted, and no query here can notice them: they have no row to be missing from.
scope.fresh_share: of the declared scope carries current evidence
scope.footnote: Nothing is in scope until somebody puts it there: a scope nobody has drawn is an undrawn scope, not the whole estate. Never scanned is counted apart from stale — a target scanned a year ago produced evidence once, one never scanned never has.
scope.load_failed: Could not load the certified scope.

owasp_grid.title: Top 10 coverage, by rule
owasp_grid.subtitle: The same ten questions answered from the finding's type alone — every mapping is one sentence you can check. Where no rule applies the answer is “covered by no scanner here”, never a guess. The report below is written by a model and is not evidence.
owasp_grid.covered: categories any scanner here can see
owasp_grid.footnote: A category with nothing found and a category nothing looks at produce the same green, which is why there are four states and not two. Code analysis places no finding: a Semgrep rule may declare its OWASP category in its own metadata, and this product does not read that metadata yet.
